vulnerabilities.title: AWS Access Key ID exposed in source
vulnerabilities.description: An AWS Access Key ID was found hardcoded in the source file. This credential grants API access to AWS services and must be rotated immediately.
vulnerabilities.solution: Remove the key from source, rotate the credential in AWS IAM, and use environment variables or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).

vulnerabilities.title: Stripe secret key hardcoded
vulnerabilities.description: A Stripe secret key (sk_live_*) was found hardcoded in the payment route. This key allows full access to your Stripe account including charges, refunds, and customer data.
vulnerabilities.solution: Revoke the key in the Stripe dashboard, issue a new one, and inject it as an environment variable at runtime.

vulnerabilities.title: JWT signing secret hardcoded
vulnerabilities.description: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded as a string literal. An attacker who reads this source can forge valid JWTs and impersonate any user including admins.
vulnerabilities.solution: Load the JWT secret from an environment variable (JWT_SECRET) and ensure it is at least 256 bits of random entropy.

vulnerabilities.title: SendGrid API key committed to repository
vulnerabilities.description: A SendGrid API key was found in the repository. This key can be used to send email on behalf of your domain, enabling phishing and spam campaigns.
vulnerabilities.solution: Revoke the key in SendGrid, rotate, and store in an environment variable or secrets manager. Add pre-commit hooks to prevent future leaks.

vulnerabilities.title: Generic API key in test fixture
vulnerabilities.description: A value matching a generic API key pattern was found in a test fixture. Even test credentials are risky if they share values with production keys or if the repo is public.
vulnerabilities.solution: Replace with obviously fake placeholder values (e.g., 'test-key-placeholder') and audit whether this value is used in any production context.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection via unsanitized user input
vulnerabilities.description: User-controlled input flows directly into a Sequelize query via string interpolation. An attacker can bypass authentication or extract the entire database with a crafted login payload.
vulnerabilities.solution: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements: `models.User.findOne({ where: { email: email } })` instead of building SQL strings manually.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via innerHTML assignment
vulnerabilities.description: User-controlled data is assigned to innerHTML without sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript into the page, stealing session tokens or performing actions on behalf of the victim.
vulnerabilities.solution: Use textContent or innerText instead of innerHTML. If HTML rendering is required, sanitize with DOMPurify before assignment.

vulnerabilities.title: Path traversal in file server route
vulnerabilities.description: The file path used in fs.readFile is constructed from an unsanitized request parameter. An attacker can request arbitrary files on the server (e.g., /etc/passwd) by encoding ../ sequences.
vulnerabilities.solution: Validate and normalize the resolved path against an allowed base directory: `if (!resolvedPath.startsWith(allowedDir)) return 403;`

vulnerabilities.title: Weak MD5 hash used for password storage
vulnerabilities.description: MD5 is used to hash user passwords. MD5 is cryptographically broken — preimage and collision attacks are practical, and rainbow table attacks trivially crack MD5 password hashes.
vulnerabilities.solution: Replace with bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2. These are purpose-built for password hashing and include work factors to resist brute force.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary code execution via eval() on user input
vulnerabilities.description: eval() is called on data derived from a user-controlled request body. This allows remote code execution — an attacker can run arbitrary server-side JavaScript.
vulnerabilities.solution: Never call eval() on external input. Parse structured data with JSON.parse() and validate the schema with a library like Zod or Joi.

vulnerabilities.title: Prototype pollution via lodash merge with user data
vulnerabilities.description: An unfiltered user-supplied object is merged into an application object using a deep-merge function. An attacker can set __proto__ properties and pollute the Object prototype, potentially leading to property injection or denial of service.
vulnerabilities.solution: Validate and whitelist incoming object keys before merging. Use Object.create(null) for accumulator objects, or use a merge library that explicitly guards against prototype pollution.

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2021-44228 — Log4Shell (log4j-core)
vulnerabilities.description: log4j-core 2.14.1 is affected by Log4Shell, one of the most severe vulnerabilities in recent history. JNDI lookup in log messages enables unauthenticated RCE via crafted user input.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade to log4j-core 2.17.1 or later. If upgrade is not immediately possible, set -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true or remove the JndiLookup class from the classpath.

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2024-6345 — Remote code execution in setuptools
vulnerabilities.description: setuptools before 70.0.0 allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted package_dir setting in a malicious package. Affects build pipelines that install from untrusted sources.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade setuptools to 70.0.0 or later: `pip install --upgrade setuptools`

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2024-4067 — ReDoS in micromatch
vulnerabilities.description: micromatch before 4.0.8 is vulnerable to a regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) via crafted glob patterns. In applications that evaluate user-supplied patterns this can cause request timeouts.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade micromatch to 4.0.8 or later. Run `npm audit fix` to apply automatically if no breaking changes exist.

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2023-44270 — CSS injection in PostCSS
vulnerabilities.description: PostCSS before 8.4.31 is vulnerable to CSS injection when parsing untrusted CSS. The parser does not correctly handle newline characters, allowing injection of unexpected CSS rules.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade postcss to 8.4.31 or later: `npm install postcss@latest`

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2023-26136 — Prototype pollution in tough-cookie
vulnerabilities.description: tough-cookie before 4.1.3 allows prototype pollution when rejectPublicSuffixes is disabled. This can be leveraged to inject arbitrary properties into Object.prototype.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade tough-cookie to 4.1.3 or later. Check if any library in your dependency tree uses tough-cookie via `npm ls tough-cookie`.

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2023-28155 — SSRF in request library
vulnerabilities.description: The deprecated `request` package is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF). An attacker may be able to redirect outbound requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.
vulnerabilities.solution: Migrate away from the unmaintained `request` library to `got`, `axios`, or the native `fetch` API. Validate and allowlist outbound URLs.

vulnerabilities.title: CVE-2024-29415 — SSRF bypass in ip package
vulnerabilities.description: The `ip` package before 2.0.1 incorrectly classifies some private IPv6 addresses as public, allowing attackers to bypass SSRF protections by using IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses.
vulnerabilities.solution: Upgrade ip to 2.0.1 or later, or replace with a maintained IP validation library. Verify SSRF guards use a library that correctly handles IPv6-mapped addresses.

vulnerabilities.title: Container runs as root user
vulnerabilities.description: No USER directive is set in the Dockerfile, so the container process runs as root (UID 0). If an attacker escapes the container, they have root privileges on the host.
vulnerabilities.solution: Add a non-root user and switch to it before the entrypoint: `RUN addgroup -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -G appgroup` followed by `USER appuser`.

vulnerabilities.title: Unpinned base image tag in Dockerfile
vulnerabilities.description: The FROM instruction uses a mutable tag (`:latest` or a non-digest reference). A future rebuild may pull a different image, introducing unexpected changes or vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities.solution: Pin the base image to a specific digest: `FROM node:20-alpine@sha256:<digest>`. Automate digest updates with Dependabot or Renovate.

vulnerabilities.title: Privileged container in Docker Compose
vulnerabilities.description: The `privileged: true` flag gives the container nearly full host kernel access, including all capabilities and device access. This effectively disables Docker's security isolation.
vulnerabilities.solution: Remove `privileged: true`. If specific capabilities are needed, grant only those using `cap_add` (e.g., `cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]`) and drop all others with `cap_drop: [ALL]`.

vulnerabilities.title: No CPU/memory limits on Kubernetes deployment
vulnerabilities.description: The container spec does not define resource requests or limits. Without limits, a compromised or misbehaving container can consume all node resources, causing a denial of service for co-located workloads.
vulnerabilities.solution:
Add resource limits and requests to the container spec:
```yaml
resources:
  requests:
    memory: "128Mi"
    cpu: "100m"
  limits:
    memory: "256Mi"
    cpu: "500m"
```

vulnerabilities.title: hostNetwork: true exposes node network to container
vulnerabilities.description: Setting hostNetwork: true causes the pod to share the node's network namespace. The container can listen on any port on the host and access all local network traffic, including traffic from other pods.
vulnerabilities.solution: Remove `hostNetwork: true` from the pod spec. If host-level network access is genuinely required, use a DaemonSet with tight RBAC and document the justification.

vulnerabilities.title: allowPrivilegeEscalation not set to false
vulnerabilities.description: The container security context does not set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false. Without this, a process inside the container can gain more privileges than its parent, for example via setuid binaries.
vulnerabilities.solution:
Add to the container securityContext:
```yaml
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  runAsNonRoot: true
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

vulnerabilities.title: apt-get install without --no-install-recommends
vulnerabilities.description: apt-get install is called without --no-install-recommends. This installs optional recommended packages, increasing image size and attack surface unnecessarily.
vulnerabilities.solution: Add the flag: `RUN apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends <packages> && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`
